# GEO in Public — Log Entry 1 **Week Zero.** This is the starting record, not a victory lap. The figures below describe implementation state and validation outputs. They do not establish a Google crawl, an index change, an answer-engine citation, traffic movement, or a causal business result. ## The standing format This is the first entry in a weekly public log of GEO work. The format will stay fixed: name the change, name the measurement, show the before and after figures, and state what the evidence does and does not support. A week with no movement belongs in the record as much as a week with a visible change. ## What changed The first release pass focused on making the site’s public source system inspectable before asking it to produce any visibility result. The work included removing legacy `noindex` directives from substantive routes, rebuilding the XML sitemap from canonical pages, adding a human-readable glossary hub, consolidating duplicate legacy paths with permanent redirects, and adding baseline Article, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList, and social metadata where the visible content supports it. The release also published two Silo I source pages: [How to Become a Source the LLMs Trust](https://masonnguyengeo.com/writing/how-to-become-source-llms-trust) and [The GEO Stack: From llms.txt to Entity Graph](https://masonnguyengeo.com/writing/geo-stack-llms-txt-to-entity-graph). Both state their claim boundaries, link primary documentation, and connect back to the glossary, ARM Framework, and AI Visibility research paths. ## What was measured The Week Zero measurements are source-system checks, not visibility claims. They came from the repository validation suite, the public sitemap response, and the recorded Search Console sitemap-submission confirmation.
Measure Before Current release state Evidence boundary
Canonical URLs in XML sitemap 8 30 Coverage of declared canonical routes, not an index count.
Legacy noindex directives on substantive routes 9 0 Source control state, not proof of crawl or index inclusion.
Technical SEO audit critical errors Not previously tracked as one release set 0 across 30 canonical routes Audit covers canonicals, index controls, metadata essentials, schema parseability, links, redirects, and sitemap parity.
Search Console sitemap submission Previous sitemap record Re-submitted successfully Submission asks Google to process the sitemap; it does not guarantee a crawl date, index count, ranking, or traffic result.
## Before / after The observable before and after is a cleaner public source map: **8 to 30 declared canonical routes** and **9 to 0 legacy noindex directives**. That is a release-state result. It tells us the crawl map is more complete and that substantive pages are no longer intentionally excluded by the old directives. It does not tell us whether Google or another system has processed those changes yet. No answer-engine citation rate, Search Console impression change, click change, crawl-frequency change, or query-level movement is reported in this entry. A defined observation window has not elapsed since the release, and publishing an invented performance figure would defeat the point of the series. ## What it means The site is now in a better position to be evaluated as a public source system: the routes are declared, the links resolve, the markup parses, the sitemap is submitted, and the research path is more explicit. That is the appropriate conclusion for Week Zero. It is too early to say whether this implementation changes search or AI-mediated discovery. The next entry should compare a fixed date window in Search Console, a documented query sample, and any captured answer-engine observations. The observation archive must retain the platform, query, date, locale or settings where relevant, result capture, and source links. ## Next measurement window The next log will document the first defined observation window after the crawl map and new Silo I pages were published. It will report the raw Search Console figures and answer-engine observations that are available, including zeroes and null results. It will separate a recorded change from an explanation for that change. > **Method note:** this series will treat visibility as an observation problem. A mention, a crawl, a click, a ranking change, and a business result are distinct events and will not be collapsed into one success claim. ## Release record - Indexability validation: 30 canonical routes, 30 sitemap URLs, zero legacy noindex directives. - Technical SEO audit: 0 critical errors and 22 metadata-length recommendations. - Production source releases: [source-record guide](https://masonnguyengeo.com/writing/how-to-become-source-llms-trust) and [GEO Stack guide](https://masonnguyengeo.com/writing/geo-stack-llms-txt-to-entity-graph). - Sitemap: [https://masonnguyengeo.com/sitemap.xml](https://masonnguyengeo.com/sitemap.xml). --- **Draft status:** ready for the scheduled August 27, 2026 publication after the first fixed observation window is captured.
